speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In 1992, we joined the Financial Action Task Force, which is an inter-governmental body that sets international standards and promotes the effective implementation of measures, to combat ML/TF and the financing of proliferation activities relating to weapons of mass destruction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: We have implemented a strong anti-money laundering and counterterrorism financing (AML/CTF) framework, in line with the international standards set by the task force.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This includes the prevention, supervision, enforcement, confiscation of proceeds of crime, and targeted financial sanctions against terrorism and proliferation financing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The financial sector and non-financial sectors, such as casinos and pawnbrokers, are subject to a comprehensive range of AML/CTF measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The financial sector, in particular, has been subject to robust supervision for many years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: ML/TF enables criminal activity to go undetected and poses serious national security concerns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: It also damages our reputation as a trusted international financial and trading centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: A robust AML/CTF framework would, therefore, benefit Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In line with the broader AML/CTF framework, we have introduced various measures to mitigate ML/TF risks in the precious stones and precious metals dealers (PSMD) sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In 2015, more comprehensive AML/CTF measures were introduced for pawnbrokers, a subset of the sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Given the inherent risks in the PSMD sector, however, there is a need to take additional and further steps.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This would also bring our regime fully in line with international standards set by the Financial Action Task Force.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: We have developed the Bill in consultation with key stakeholders through, firstly, a survey of the industry; secondly, consultations with industry associations, such as the Singapore Jewellers Association, the Diamond Exchange of Singapore, as well as the Singapore Bullion Market Association; and finally, through a public consultation held between 13 September and 12 October 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In response to the feedback received, we have streamlined the requirements in the Bill to manage regulatory and compliance costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: We have also benchmarked the requirements against practices in other jurisdictions, such as the United Kingdom (UK) and also Belgium.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Bill provides, firstly, for the appointment of a Registrar to supervise the PSMD sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Thirdly, it provides for investigation and enforcement powers, as well as prescription of penalties for failure to abide by the requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Bill provides for the regulation of any person who carries on a business of regulated dealing or a business as an intermediary for regulated dealing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This includes persons involved in the manufacturing, importing or possessing for sale, and selling or offering for sale any precious stone, precious metal or precious product.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: These persons are currently subject to the cash transaction reporting regime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Bill will impose additional measures on these classes of dealers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Bill goes further to include: (a) the sale or redemption of asset-backed tokens, which are instruments backed by precious stones, metals or products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Such tokens may be used for ML/TF as they are good stores of value; (b) the purchase of precious stones, precious metals or precious products from a customer for the purpose of resale, as these items may be proceeds from crime or used as means for ML/TF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Intermediaries, such as auction houses and providers of trading platforms services for PSMD, whether by electronic means or otherwise, are also covered under the regime, as they facilitate transactions between buyers and sellers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Regulating these intermediaries will prevent such transactions from being used for ML/TF purposes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Clause 4 of the Bill provides for the Minister to appoint a Registrar, Deputy Registrars and Assistant Registrars, to supervise the PSMD sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Regulated dealers, unless exempted, must register with the Registrar, in order to carry out the regulated dealing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Clause 7 of the Bill provides that the Registrar may refuse to grant or refuse to renew registration, under certain circumstances, for example, if applicants were convicted of offences, such as those involving fraud, dishonesty or money laundering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This will help ensure that individuals who are not fit and proper do not operate as regulated dealers in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Clause 9 of the Bill provides for the Registrar to impose conditions of registration on registered dealers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Conditions which may be imposed include the requirement to inform the Registrar of changes to registration details, to ensure that registered dealers remain fit and proper.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Registrar may cancel or suspend the registration of dealers under certain circumstances, for example, if the registered dealer fails to comply with any condition of registration, or if the registered dealer is no longer a fit and proper person.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Part 3 of the Bill sets out the measures for prevention of money laundering and financing of terrorism which will apply to all regulated dealers who carry out any part of their business of regulated dealing or business as an intermediary for regulated dealing in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The requirements are broadly categorised as transaction-based or entity-based.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Clause 17 which requires regulated dealers to submit a copy of the cash transaction report to the Registrar, in addition to existing requirements to file cash transaction reports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Clause 18 which requires regulated dealers to keep records of transactions where CDD measures are performed and information obtained through these CDD measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Clause 21 which requires regulated dealers to submit a copy of the information of suspicious transactions to the Registrar, in addition to the existing requirement already under the CDSA to disclose suspicious transactions and also under the Terrorism (Suppression of Financing) Act to report terrorism financing information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In line with the risk-based approach to prevent ML/TF, businesses will only be required to develop procedures to address the risks identified in their risk assessment, in addition to the principal obligations prescribed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Taking in feedback from the public consultation, we have streamlined the principal obligations provided in the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: We will also provide guidance on the obligations and procedures to address the varying degrees and levels of risks, to help regulated dealers mitigate risks of ML/TF whilst, at the same time, also managing compliance costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Registrar may give written directions to regulated dealers under certain circumstances, such as to stop a particular employee who has been negligent in performing AML/CTF measures on multiple occasions from conducting any part of the regulated dealer’s business.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This is necessary to enable the Registrar to immediately address any activity which contravenes requirements in the Bill or which may pose an ML/TF risk.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Bill provides the Registrar with powers of inspection and monitoring, investigation and seizure of property, to deal with possible contraventions of the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This is also in line with penalties introduced in other Acts, such as the Pawnbrokers Act, as the culpability of persons who commit ML/TF offences would be similar.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Clause 38 of the Bill provides for the Minister to exempt any person or class of persons, or any activity, from any provision of the Bill, subject to conditions or restrictions specified.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This allows regulated dealers who are already covered under other AML/CTF regimes to be exempted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: For example, it is intended for all Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS)-regulated financial institutions to be exempted from registration and AML/CTF requirements under the Bill, where they are already subjected to MAS regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Classes of financial institutions that conduct regulated dealing, for example, banks, insurers, stored value facilities, will continue to be supervised by MAS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Registrar will also work with the industry, including conducting outreach to raise AML/CTF awareness as well as issuing guidance to regulated dealers, to ensure that they are well-placed to comply with the new requirements proposed in this Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This will help us to better manage ML/TF risks, and combat crime and improve security both domestically and globally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: It will also reaffirm our commitment to be a responsible member of the international community, upholding our status as a well-regarded and well-regulated financial centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: With that, Mr Speaker, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As the way these syndicates and perpetrators work is dynamic, it is important not to leave a gap in our preventive framework which they can exploit.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, this Bill is timely to bolster our AML/CTF measures by increasing the standard of such practices in the industry, and, also, to protect the many hardworking merchants who operate within the industry.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Precious stones and precious minerals are highly valued yet relatively compact, making it easy and desirable to store or smuggle.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Their worldwide demand makes it easy to convert their value into money and vice versa.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Their form is versatile and easily changed, making it difficult to trace.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For instance, in "Operation Meltdown" overseen by the United States (US) Homeland Security Investigations, proceeds from drug trafficking were money laundered through gold.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Part of the scheme involved converting gold bullion into nuts, bolts and other items, enabling them to declare them as “gold pigment".

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I have a few questions on the scope of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: From paragraph (e) of the definition of "regulated dealing" under clause 2, this Bill seeks to regulate the purchasing of precious stones, precious mineral or precious product for the purpose of resale.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Would it include individuals who buy precious stones and precious minerals who make a one-off sale, for instance, to the pawnshop?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: What if there is more than one purpose for purchase?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For instance, gold pieces are often bought during wedding preparation both as a gift and also as an investment.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Would that be considered purchase for the purpose of resale?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Also, what kinds of situations is paragraph (b) involving "intermediary" envisaged to cover?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If the value is referring to retail value, how will it be determined whether 50% of the value is attributable to precious stone or precious material or to the branding of a product or the craftsmanship that goes into it?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As luxury brands may carry a range of products – some with precious stones and precious metals which may fall under regulated dealing, it is necessary that there be sufficient clarity and guidance on what is or is not a precious product.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Clarity is important for compliance and effective regulation, yet it is also vital that these new regulations do not unduly curb in businesses' creativity when designing products.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For instance, if a manufacturer based overseas buys scrap metal from Singapore, would that overseas manufacturer require registration?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This Bill adopts a risk-based approach to regulation.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is good because of ML/TF, both dynamic, always looking for new loopholes to exploit.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The common fundamental principle running through the whole variety of players in the precious stones and precious minerals industry is that of identifying and addressing risks appropriately.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: How that works for each business may differ.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For instance, the kinds of risk that a person in the scrap metal business faces and a jeweller faces are different.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As such, it is important that the objective is clear and expectations communicated so that each of the different sectors can comply meaningfully.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: There needs to be input from each sector of the industry so that the guidelines will make sense for the kinds of situations they may face.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This Bill will help ease the transition of working current informal checking processes into a regulatory framework that is sensible and robust.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Further, there needs to be training and education so that regulated dealers and their employees will be able to effectively implement the appropriate guidelines.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If the regulated dealers understand the process but are unable to articulate it to the employees, the regulatory framework will not be as effectively implemented.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: These guidelines need to be flexible enough to allow discretion to be applied to individual situations, yet they need to provide sufficient guidance for them to be effective.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The idea is not to be too burdensome for legitimate transactions but, at the same time, be sufficiently robust to identify and deter illegitimate transactions.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As the effects of this Bill will be felt at all levels of the precious metal and precious stones market, including the individual buyers, AML/CTF needs to be an ongoing conversation requiring regulator-industry cooperation.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For instance, there are concerns that customers will not understand why identity or proof of ownership may be important.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Some customers may feel uncomfortable, threatened or put off by needing to answer so many questions.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Lack of understanding of certain terms used in risk-profiling, such as "politically exposed persons" (PEP), may also be a hindrance to obtaining the requisite information.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: These concerns of regulated dealers overstepping and intruding into customers' details unnecessarily cannot be treated lightly.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: To this end, what will be done to raise awareness among the general public about what to expect and the importance of such processes?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: How will regulated dealers be supported in complying with the guidelines, for instance, giving them the power to ask for certain private information or building capacity so that they will be able to search in the relevant "watchlists" should such actions become necessary?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Further, what will be done to address concerns that private information will not be obtained unnecessarily and that private information obtained will remain secure and confidential if eventually not needed for any AML/CTF investigations?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Singapore's position as a major financial hub brings with it greater exposure to transnational economic crime.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: To counteract this, Singapore has developed and implemented a robust AML/CTF framework to target, prevent and confiscate the proceeds of crime, particularly within the financial sector, and the Senior Minister of State has mentioned some aspects of it in his earlier speech.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This House had, as recently as in October last year, passed the Serious Crimes and Counter-Terrorism Bill, to strengthen our ability to detect and deter criminals.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Apart from the financial sector, other designated non-financial sectors, such as pawnbrokers, are also subject to AML/CTF measures.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: However, we are only as safe and strong as our weakest link.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is a gap that criminals may exploit and may even be presently exploiting.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The PSMD sector is particularly vulnerable, as identified by Mr Christopher de Souza, because of the fact that precious stones and metals are easily transported, concealed and converted into cash.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This can be used by criminals to launder monies to hide their illicit sources of funds.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The payments were first made by way of a telegraphic transfer from his firm’s client account and, subsequently, a cash cheque was issued in the name of the firm’s client account.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: His clients subsequently tried to recover their losses from the jeweller via a civil action before the Singapore Courts.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In doing so, the clients alleged that the jeweller ought to have known from the circumstances of the transactions that he was using monies belonging to another in breach of trust.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The Singapore Court of Appeal, in its 2010 decision, considered that whilst there were some circumstances surrounding the transaction which arguably might have raised cause for concern about the probity of the transaction, the jeweller did not cross the boundaries of reasonable commercial conduct in relation to the first transaction paid through telegraphic transfer of monies.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In arriving at its decision, a key consideration of the Court of Appeal was that there was no pre-existing practice of jewellers questioning customers on the source of funds, such that it would not be fair to criticise the jeweller’s staff for their failure to query the source of purchaser’s funds.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The Court of Appeal's comments in this regard were particularly pertinent and exemplifies the gap in our present regulatory scheme.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It said: "Clearly, it is not the usual practice for jewellers and retailers, in general, to ask their clients searching questions about the source of their funds.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: As rightly pointed out by the Judge, indeed, there are usually cogent reasons for not asking questions.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Genuine clients would feel offended, the transaction might be unreasonably delayed, and costs incurred.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Admittedly, in certain types of commercial transactions, there might well be a practice of exercising due diligence…In Singapore, unlike the US and the UK, there are currently no rules that require jewellers, gem dealers and precious metal dealers to implement anti-money laundering programmes… ...This is why the Judge quite correctly remarked that most honest retailers would not bother to check on the background or standing of their customers even for very large purchases; there is simply no general practice of making inquiries and imposing such an invariable requirement on large transactions might jeopardise completion of large numbers of legitimate transactions." If the jeweller in question had been required to conduct due diligence checks on the source of funds, perhaps this unfortunate matter might have been prevented.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I welcome the Bill, which will shore up our defences against financial crime.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I also applaud the fact that the Ministry of Law had conducted public consultation and incorporated the feedback into the Bill that is being introduced in the House today for Second Reading.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I take the opportunity to make a few short comments on the proposed Bill.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The first area concerns how the Ministry intends to ensure that jewellers, bullion traders, jewellery wholesalers and retailers, auctioneers and secondhand goods dealers – who would be regulated dealers under the Bill – would be adequately equipped to understand their obligations under the Bill, such as their obligations to conduct CDD and filing of suspicious transaction reports.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Such dealers may be tradesmen who may not be familiar with or have experience in carrying out such AML controls, or whose current business models would need to be adapted to allow such controls to be implemented.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: What are some of the steps that the Ministry has taken or plans to take to ensure that regulated dealers will have the necessary training and will be well-versed with their obligations under the Bill and understand the consequences of non-compliance, for example, via ongoing industry engagements through industry bodies, such as the Singapore Jewellers Association?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Next, it should also be noted that PSMDs are generally not as well-resourced as banks.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Would the Ministry be providing support to enable PSMDs to build capacity to conduct CDD?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In comparison, I recall it was announced that MAS was working with the banking sector to develop a common screening platform for CDD purposes.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It may not be practical to require PSMDs to share information of purchasers’ identities with their competitors.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: But on the other hand, there could be scope for pooling information amongst affiliated PSMDs or outlets of the same PSMDs.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I welcome the Senior Minister of State's clarification on this.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The Bill does not specify what this period of time is, save to say that the different periods may be prescribed for different classes of regulated dealers, different types of designated transactions or different documents and information.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Presumably, these requirements will be specified through secondary legislation.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Could the Senior Minister of State please provide some guidance as to what the prescribed period of time would likely be?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: What are the considerations behind the need to segregate the prescribed period based on different classes of dealers or transactions?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, it refers, for example, to companies, partnerships and sole proprietorships which sell precious metals, stones and products, such as jewellery.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Christopher de Souza also asked whether the definition of "regulated dealing" covers purchases of precious stones, metals and products for multiple purposes, including for the purpose of resale.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is not the intention of the regime to cover individuals who make one-off purchases and subsequently may decide then at some stage to sell their items to a second-hand goods dealer.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Whilst such activities may be carried on for the purposes of gain, these are conceivably not matters that fall within the definition of "business".

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But, of course, if this happens once too often and there is a pattern of such activity, then all of that would be taken into account when looked at and considered in the context of the definition as to whether there is activity that generates gain under the definition.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, from the individual's perspective, I have addressed Mr Christopher de Souza's point, but from the perspective of the regulated dealers, as well as those who purchase the second-hand items from these individuals, they would have to perform the AML/CTF measures where appropriate.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On intermediaries, Mr Christopher de Souza asked what situations specific to limb B of the definition of regulated dealings involving intermediaries do we envisage we would cover.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Intermediaries, as defined in clause 2 of the Bill, such as precious stones and metals exchange or auctioneer, would be covered under the Bill, and we need to cover the intermediaries because, otherwise, the intermediaries would immediately provide a way in which you would enable anonymity in the transactions, if one uses the intermediary to deal with the transactions in these precious stones or metals.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Such intermediaries may import the items from overseas suppliers and perform the sale in Singapore on behalf of their overseas suppliers.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Depending on the mode of transaction through the intermediary, it may not be possible for suppliers to perform the AML/CTF measures required, for example, to verify the identity of the customer.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is, therefore, necessary to also regulate intermediaries to ensure that the appropriate AML/CTF measures are performed where necessary.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked if the Bill applies to persons or businesses based overseas but engaged in dealing with regulated dealers in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, the touchstone is that, if the business is carried on in Singapore, it will apply to them.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the example that Mr de Souza cited, the manufacturers based overseas would not have to register with the Ministry or comply with the requirements of the regime when purchasing scrap metal from Singapore as long as he does not carry out any part of his business of regulated dealing in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Nevertheless, such dealers will be subject, of course, to the relevant AML/CTF verifications and processes in their home jurisdictions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr de Souza asked how the Ministry will determine if a product is a precious product.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There is a lot of subjectivity to that.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But as Mr de Souza also mentioned, there needs to be a degree of flexibility in the way we look at this.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Obviously, if one is too prescriptive with the definition, then the effects of the Bill will lose its flexibility and that may then allow a loophole to be introduced.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Having said that, we recognise that precious products may have different parameters to determine their value beyond just the value of the stones and metals, for example, in the branding or craftsmanship of such products.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In cases where the classification of precious products is not immediately apparent, we will, of course, work with the industry to determine if they ought to be considered as precious products and then provide the necessary guidance to the rest of the industry.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On that score, I recognise both Mr Murali Pillai and Mr de Souza raising the point that we need to have more communication between the regulator and the regulated and that, obviously, would be done as we embark on this journey after the Bill is passed.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On multiple transactions, Mr Murali Pillai asked how the Ministry would handle customers who spread the transactions over time, flying under the radar and keeping the transactions below the $20,000 threshold.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is an existing requirement under the Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) Act.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is possible for customers to transact with multiple, not just one, but multiple different regulated dealers and go below the threshold each time, to avoid the CDD checks.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: However, the threshold itself is designed to make it difficult for criminals to misuse regulated dealers for illicit purposes, by introducing a degree of friction in the system in a way in which the transactions would be done.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Should dealers come across any suspicious transactions, they also have to report it to the Suspicious Transactions Reporting Office (STRO) in accordance with already prevailing existing requirements.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will not expect regulated dealers to share their customers' information with their competitors, obviously.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As the Member Mr Murali Pillai pointed out, that may not be practical.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But he has raised an interesting suggestion about how some of the information could be pooled within or amongst the affiliated dealers or outlets of the same PSMD and that might be a better way to try to link the different transactions should such an occurrence of multiple transactions occur.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is similar to the record-keeping requirement imposed by all other sectors, including pawnbrokers, and is also aligned with the international standards set by the Financial Action Task Force.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked for the rationale behind the power to prescribe different time periods for different classes of dealers or transactions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is needed because the level of ML/TF risk posed by different classes of dealers or transactions may itself require different time periods for the records to be kept.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I just want to touch on how we intend to support the industry, because that is obviously a very relevant question that both Members have raised.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To start off, as I have mentioned earlier, we had engaged stakeholders early on, even before we formulated this Bill, to better understand the mechanics of the sector, how it works, what would be the issues that they face on the ground and what is needed to build the capacity to comply with the relevant requirements.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These stakeholders, as I mentioned earlier, would include the Singapore Jewellers Association, and the Singapore Bullion Market Association and so on.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: During the public consultation, we also held briefings and dialogues for industry associations to explain and clarify the requirements of the regime.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Moving forward, we will continue to work with these industry associations to engage regulated dealers to help them comply – first of all, understand, and thereafter also comply, with the requirements of the regime.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And we intend to do it through regular AML/CTF seminars, outreach sessions and dialogues for the dealers, and the first session will likely be held when registration commences.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These will include details on how to perform proper CDD, how to perform risk assessments and implement internal policies, procedures and controls.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And based on feedback from associations, we will also, where appropriate, provide the materials in different languages and issue templates and checklists, so as to help the ground and the smaller players within this sector to better appreciate and also implement these measures.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For instance, we will issue a brochure which will contain information on the registration process to regulated dealers before registration commences.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We agree with Mr de Souza that the ML/TF risks faced by the sub-sectors within the industry may differ.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There is not necessarily parity within the different sub-sectors and we will work with these sub-sectors and industry associations to support them and also develop guidelines which may be specific to their needs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr de Souza asked if regulated dealers will be given the power to ask for private information.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In general, regulated dealers are not prohibited from collecting, using or disclosing personal data as long as it is strictly required for compliance with the requirements in this Bill.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: However, that said, regulated dealers are required to ensure that reasonable security arrangements are in place to protect personal data in their possession or under their control.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That is really no different from the current regime, anyway.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Other than complying with the requirements in the Bill, regulated dealers also have to comply with the Personal Data Protection Act and ensure that personal information obtained is not used or disclosed for other purposes, such as marketing, without the consent of the customer.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Where appropriate, we will also be issuing guidance on how personal information should be obtained, handled and stored.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr de Souza asked what will be done to raise awareness amongst the general public about the new requirements of the regime and the importance of such processes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Those are very good points, and we will work with the industry to inform the public of the importance and requirements of the regime, in particular, the need to obtain customer’s personal information as part of that due diligence exercise, so as to facilitate regulated dealers in their compliance with the regime.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, we may also consider issuing posters and other guidance notes on the new requirements for regulated dealers to put up in their places of business.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They pose significant social, security and reputational concerns.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To address these concerns, Singapore has implemented a strong AML/CTF framework for the financial and non-financial sectors.
